label: NASA · verified context
title: Travel to Mars: generally 7–10 months
use: Engine accepts direct transfers only within 210–300 days (30-day educational months). Route duration drives elapsed hours, cumulative energy and environmental exposure. Exact 272/288-day scenarios are team inputs, not independently verified ephemerides.

label: ESA · verified context
title: Radio signals: about 4–24 minutes one way
use: The model interpolates 4–24 minutes. Event decisions compare round-trip delay with a 20-minute response window. A stronger antenna changes throughput, not light speed.

label: JPL · design inspiration
title: Concept Maturity Levels
use: CML-inspired preparation milestones. In-game criteria and grants are fictional, not official CML certification.

label: Team · provisional model
title: Equipment, routes and biological model
use: 800 W resolves the 700/800 W conflict using the final team table. Costs, launchers, linear delta-v penalty, 85% cruise-power factor, 1600 Wh battery, 128 MB storage, 2.5 °C/70% RH targets and all risk thresholds are gameplay assumptions. Exact route query provenance remains unverified. Venus 352-day transfer is outside the 7–10-month MVP.

label: Open scientific question
title: Dormant bumblebee queens in interplanetary flight
use: Risk is an educational index, never a survival probability. No claim is made that bumblebees can survive transport to Mars. Arrival ends the MVP: no landing, colony or pollination is simulated.
